exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: Other meanings from the prefix table: вы- — Step out for a short period of time: Секретарь вышел на десять минут. — The secretary left for ten minutes. под- — Подвезти – give someone a lift: Он подвёз меня до центра. — He took me (as far as) downtown. от- — With transitive verbs, delivering or dropping something off (agent does not remain): Я отнесу книги в библиотеку, потом приду. — I'll drop the book off at the library, then come. до- — Characterizing the duration of a journey, especially when it is long: Мы наконец доехали до дачи. — We finally reached the dacha. пере- — Changing residence: Я переехала в другой город. — I moved to another city. про- — Movement beyond one's destination (possibly unintentional): Я боюсь, что мы уже прошли магазин. — I'm afraid we already passed the store. на- — Quantified movement: Водитель наездил 50 километров. — The driver covered 50 kilometers. — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Other meanings from the prefix table: вы- — Step out for a short period of time: Секретарь вышел на десять минут. — The secretary left for ten minutes. под- — Подвезти – give someone a lift: Он подвёз меня до центра. — He took me (as far as) downtown.…

exercises.why: **привести / приводить** — to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce. **довести / доводить** — to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald; to drive, to reduce, to bring, to carry. **завести / заводить** — to take, to bring, to lead; to get, to procure, to acquire, to buy; to establish, to set up, to found; to start. **нанести / наносить** — to drift (on); to carry, to waft, to deposit, to wash ashore (e.g. of snow, sand, etc.); to mark (on); to draw (e.g. onto a map); to inflict (on); to cause (to); to bring. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: привести / приводить — to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce.

exercises.why: **выйти / выходить** — to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out. — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Oshtylech is marrying on the day after tomorrow.
exercises.context: выйти / выходить — to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out.
